channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Putin rejects mobilization rumors, many Russians unconvinced
item.description: Russia’s President Vladimir Putin has dismissed rumors about military mobilization. But many Russians, including many DW users, say they are preparing for the possibility.

item.title: [ECFR] A future with Chinese characteristics
item.description: The world is undergoing a historical and cultural rupture. Just as Hollywood and other American exports once gave the rest of the world a glimpse of modern life and the future that awaited them, China is now doing the same for African, Latin American and even American young people

item.title: [ECFR] Friends without benefits: Why the EU should offer Canada more than casual defence ties
item.description: Trump is pushing Canada—a quiet military powerhouse—away from America. The EU should seize the chance and fold it into its own defence

item.title: [DW] German economy frets about Saxony-Anhalt election results
item.description: The AfD won the election in the eastern German state by a wide margin. While politicians and election analysts are still debating the reasons for the far-right party's popularity, economists are sounding the alarm.

item.title: [DW] Ratko Mladic’s funeral casts shadow over Bosnia and Herzegovina vote
item.description: Ratko Mladic’s funeral in Belgrade, attended by Serbian and Bosnian Serb leaders, has deepened regional tensions and could affect the upcoming election in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

item.title: [ECFR] Future nostalgia: Europe’s unfinished song
item.description: ECFR’s new research reveals Europeans are suffering from an imagination gap. Many people want to see Europe strong and flourishing—but fewer can picture a credible route from today’s disruptions to that destination

item.title: [ECFR] Beyond Saxony-Anhalt: What Merz’s crisis means for Europe
item.description: The far-right AfD’s win in a small German state calls for dynamism in Berlin and hedging in Brussels

item.title: [ECFR] Emergency Room: The AfD’s victory in Saxony-Anhalt
item.description: Mark Leonard welcomes Jana Puglierin, senior policy fellow and head of ECFR’s Berlin office, to discuss the Alternative for Germany (AfD)’s election win in Saxony-Anhalt—and what it means for Germany and Europe

item.title: [ECFR] Britons back ban on trade with Israeli settlements by more than two to one
item.description: New polling published by ECFR shows that Britons across the political divide favour banning trade with illegal Israeli settlements

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘She killed me with her post’: Gaza students caught in Belgian minister’s immigration posturing
item.description: Belgium's immigration minister has gone on the warpath against evacuating 13 students from Gaza, but they might still be flying out despite her anti-Arab and pro-Israel dog-whistling.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukraine’s financial crisis resurrects Europe’s bitter dilemma on Russian frozen assets
item.description: The dire financial situation of Ukraine, ahead of what is expected to be a difficult winter with a possible further Russian mobilisation, has reopened the discussion on whether to use Russian frozen assets — raising difficult questions over legality, financial stability and Europe’s leverage in any future peace deal.

item.title: [DW] Germany’s Goethe-Institut is closing in Russia. Russians tell DW how canceled exams are upending their plans
item.description: Canceled language exams, disrupted plans to study in Germany and the disappearance of an important cultural link: DW users shared how the closure of Germany's Goethe-Institut in Russia affects their lives.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU asylum claims drop to lowest level in five years, but many still lost at sea
item.description: Despite increased calls to curb migration, asylum application numbers have been following a downward trend, due to geopolitical circumstances and EU cooperation with third countries. Migrants deaths on the journey, however, are far from dropping.

item.title: [EU Observer] Cleared in Greek border case, Austrian activist now sues EU data chief over Europol record
item.description: An Austrian national who helped document rights violations at the Greek Turkey border in 2020 is suing the EU's data protection watchdog over allegations it failed to protect her rights after Europol collected her personal information amid a Greek criminal case, for which she was later exonerated.

item.title: [EU Observer] ECB raises rates again as Strait of Hormuz disruption drives up gas prices
item.description: The conflict in the Middle East has pushed up energy-related inflation by 14.3 percent year-on-year

item.title: [DW] Are electric cars really bad for the environment?
item.description: Some German politicians are calling for a delay to the EU plan to phase out gas-powered vehicles, saying cars must be judged on the entire carbon footprint. But the full picture still says EVs are more climate friendly.

item.title: [ECFR] Booted, then suited: Veterans and the making of Putin’s new proto-elite
item.description: The Kremlin is promoting Ukraine war veterans--cultivating a proto-elite who could reinforce Russia’s militarised course.

item.title: [DW] Serbia, the conflicted EU candidate
item.description: On paper, Belgrade has pursued EU membership for years. But accession has long been stalled. The hero's farewell given to war criminal Mladic exposed just how far Serbia has alienated itself from Europe.

item.title: [DW] US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold Ukraine talks after meeting Putin
item.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv, seeking to revive efforts to end the war. But the latest diplomatic push seems to have produced no breakthrough.

item.title: [DW] Germany, Kosovo unite against ticks carrying deadly virus
item.description: Germany has high-security labs while Kosovo has Hyalomma ticks and experience with the deadly Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever. Working together, German and Kosovar scientists are fighting the disease and its vectors.

item.title: [DW] Hungary begins hunt for corrupt regime's billions
item.description: Hungary's new prime minister promised he would recover billions stolen or diverted by the previous administration. A new "super authority" is about to begin that work. Its success or failure will have a big impact.

item.title: [Financial Times] Saudi Arabia shuts East-West pipeline that bypasses Hormuz after attacks
item.description: Move is likely to put further momentum behind fast-rising oil prices

item.title: [Politico Europe] Trump says he would ‘love’ to see a united Ireland
item.description: "It's going to happen eventually", the U.S. president said in Dublin during a golf-focused trip to the long-divided island.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Farage’s Reform UK gets £36m from crypto billionaire
item.description: It is the largest single donation ever received by a British political party.

item.title: [Financial Times] Canada seeks $1tn from investors looking for a haven from Trump
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney hosts a summit to put money behind his plan to decouple from an increasingly hostile US

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Could musicians and dancers in Europe revolt against AI using their work? ‘It should be possible’, says performing arts boss
item.description: Performers of works authored by others are in a particularly precarious position when it comes to AI training on their work. How can the EU protect them?

item.title: [EU Observer] Not every incident is Russian sabotage. But it suits the defence sector to say so
item.description: Europe’s challenge is not only to protect critical infrastructure and deter Russian aggression, but also to maintain credibility by clearly establishing what Russia has actually done.

item.title: [Politico Europe] OpenAI reveals another rogue AI attack
[DW] Russia's drone war comes to Moldova and Romania
item.description: Incursions by Russian drones into Moldovan and Romanian airspace are increasingly common. This week the Ukrainian president's plane was stopped from taking off from Chisinau. Observers suspect the attacks are deliberate.

item.title: [DW] DW exclusive: Zelenskyy offers to meet Putin at G20 in Miami
item.description: In an interview with DW, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country was in a strong position to negotiate and offered to meet Vladimir Putin in Miami.

item.title: [Financial Times] We are setting up a generation to fail at school
item.description: The disturbing global decline in test results rests on wrong-headed curriculum changes

item.title: [Financial Times] Booming Brics payments systems seek more cross-border links
item.description: Government-backed networks such as UPI and Pix explore link-ups with central banks overseas

item.title: [Financial Times] US limits air defence time slots for tankers sailing through Hormuz
item.description: Shift to two specified times daily follows increase in Iranian attacks

item.title: [Financial Times] EU races to Le Pen-proof its agenda
item.description: Diplomats say Paris has urged bloc to agree budget and climate measures before French presidential election in April

item.title: [Politico Europe] Portugal wants EU cash to pay for firefighting goats
item.description: As budget negotiations intensify, capitals are reaching for a new argument to keep money in the farming pot: climate change.

item.title: [Financial Times] Larry Ellison to sell up to $7.5bn worth of Oracle stock
item.description: Founder to offload as many as 50mn shares as company posts higher revenue from data centres but faces investor fears it is overcommitted to AI

item.title: [DW] War criminal Ratko Mladic buried with military honors in Belgrade, Serbia
item.description: Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb commander convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, has been buried in Belgrade. The funeral, broadcast live on TV, comes just days before President Vucic is expected to call an election.

item.title: [ECFR] Against war, drought and hunger: A global coalition to prevent a food crisis
item.description: Three features of today’s unordered world are converging to create a devastating food crisis. Russia’s war in Ukraine is disrupting agricultural exports from both countries. The enduring blockage of the Strait of Hormuz is restricting fertiliser shipments. And this year’s El Niño (a sporadic warming of the Pacific Ocean generating widespread knock-on effects elsewhere) could […]

item.title: [DW] Outrage as Maltese tycoon acquitted in journalist's murder
item.description: Maltese businessman Yorgen Fenech has been found not guilty of complicity to murder journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. Almost nine years after the attack, the question of who ordered her death remains unanswered.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU delays key tobacco tax vote until after Swedish election
item.description: Sweden has blocked the legislation over opposition to taxing nicotine pouches.

item.title: [Politico Europe] ‘I don’t have any’: Trump brushes aside concerns over AI’s existential risks
item.description: The president is instead focusing on American tech maintaining its lead over China.

item.title: [Financial Times] Why the AI race has its creators fearing human extinction
item.description: Advances in autonomous agents and bitter rivalry between Anthropic and OpenAI have pushed once-fringe fears into the mainstream

item.title: [Politico Europe] Escaping the AI safety nightmare: What can governments do?
item.description: Heightened global AI safety panic is leading to louder calls for regulation.

item.title: [Financial Times] How both sides lost after 9/11
item.description: America lost wars and Osama bin Laden lost Saudi Arabia

item.title: [Politico Europe] Trump, Hegseth push Iran war at Pentagon 9/11 memorial
item.description: “We are ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon,” Hegseth said.

item.title: [Politico Europe] ‘Abuse of power’: Von der Leyen rapped after backing space mega deal
item.description: The European Parliament’s leading competition lawmaker accuses the Commission chief of pre-empting merger review.

item.title: [EU Observer] Belgium’s foreign minister accuses coalition of ‘blackmail’ for blocking 13 Gaza students
item.description: "Faced with this situation, where issues were being held hostage at the expense of people's suffering, I chose to withdraw my proposal. Dignity is not for sale," said Belgium's normally mild-mannered foreign minister.

item.title: [ECFR] Remembering Emma Bonino
item.description: ECFR founding member and co-chair emerita Emma Bonino has died at the age of 78. A towering figure in European foreign policy, she was an inspiration to millions across the continent. She left a deep mark on European and Italian politics, and on ECFR

item.title: [ECFR] The EU’s unfinished business in the Western Balkans
item.description: Montenegro and Albania are moving closer to EU membership. But Brussels should not forget its responsibility towards the Western Balkans as a whole

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘Not everyone wants to come to Europe’, says IOM researcher warning against migration panic
item.description: From who cares for Europe’s elderly to who picks its crops, Pablo Rojas Coppari argues that closing regular migration routes today will silently undercut the continent’s own ageing societies tomorrow.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Sweden’s NATO missions are at risk if the left wins election, warns PM Kristersson
item.description: The center-right leader told POLITICO that Magdalena Andersson’s political partners can’t be trusted on defense.

item.title: [EU Observer] Anthropic AI has joined the Ukraine war, after Russia took advantage (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,660)
item.description: Russia’s use of a Western AI model to probe Ukrainian defences and automate drone warfare exposes a new front where Silicon Valley tools now shape risks and leverage in Europe’s largest war.

item.title: [EU Observer] Victims of online harm fear von der Leyen will backtrack on child social‑media ban
item.description: This year's State of the Union address was expected to contain social media restrictions to greater safeguard children in light of sustained harm, and sometimes, deaths. Recently, however, Ursula von der Leyen's tune seems to have changed.

item.title: [EU Observer] Lead centre-right MEP suggests softening emissions-trading to help ‘suffering’ industries
item.description: The lead MEP on Emissions Trading Scheme reform has set out plans to soften the EU Commission's draft and give industries more time to adjust.

item.title: [DW] Turks in Germany anxious after AfD wins in Saxony-Anhalt
item.description: The Alternative for Germany party's win in Saxony-Anhalt has alarmed people of Turkish origin in eastern states. Will workers and business owners abandon the increasingly AfD-friendly region for the more welcoming west?

item.title: [EU Observer] 25 years after 9/11, have the terrorists won?
item.description: As Donald Trump gambles on chaos at home and Vladimir Putin’s missiles pound Ukrainian cities, Timothy Snyder warns that Americans now face a new, self-inflicted 9/11-style test of whether they will - again - react exactly as the terrorists hope.

item.title: [EU Observer] Magyar’s Hungary expels 10 Russian diplomats and dismantles Fidesz’s county fiefdoms (Day 122 of the Tisza government)
item.description: By slashing the powers of Fidesz’s regional barons and kicking out a fifth of Russia’s embassy staff, Péter Magyar is trying to recast Hungary’s role in both its own hinterland and the wider European security game.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: How Sweden’s tight election could normalise far-right power-sharing across Europe
item.description: With two blocs neck-and-neck, Sweden’s election could cement a new model in Europe where mainstream conservatives openly govern with the far right, reshaping EU debates on migration, energy and security.

item.title: [DW] Magyar vs. Moscow: Hungary toughens stance toward Russia
item.description: Prime Minister Peter Magyar has abruptly ended the era of his predecessor's warm relations with Russia: Hungary has expelled 10 Russian diplomats. The Kremlin is considering halting gas supplies in response.

item.title: [ECFR] Ukraine: The battle beyond war
item.description: Jessica Hendrick welcomes Roman Petrov and Svitlana Zalishchuk to discuss Ukraine’s simultaneous fight for survival on the frontlines and battle for democracy at home

item.title: [ECFR] The geopolitics of global hunger
item.description: Mark Leonard welcomes Cary Fowler and Jim O’Brien to discuss the factors behind the escalating risk of a major food crisis—and Europe’s role in preventing catastrophe

item.title: [ECFR] Orchestrators, not customers: A new role for European governments in defence
item.description: Weapons that took decades to develop can now be countered within months. European governments need to stop buying finished platforms and start running an innovation cycle, in which soldiers learn from one system and build these lessons into the next

item.title: [ECFR] Bonus episode: The EU enlargement game
item.description: In a special episode recorded live from Lisbon, Jessica Hendrick puts six EU candidate countries through an enlargement simulation to find out what happens when crisis, cash, disinformation and political pressure collide with the race to join the EU

item.title: [ECFR] A no to the EU, not to Europe: What Icelanders actually voted on
item.description: Icelanders voted no because of old, domestic reasons: fish, the currency and comfort with the status quo. The result was not a victory for the far-right—but the heated campaign is a warning sign for Icelandic political life.
